street.gap_assumption: No management margin target, so there is no gap to compute. D is scored on the no-level rule: the 4-month forward EBITDA revision is -1.3% (between -3% and +5%). Consensus already models recovery from the LTM 15.5% to 17.2% in FY2026 and 18.1% in FY2028 (calendar years).

evidence_of_progress.note: VA EBITDA margin: Q4 2025 13.43% vs 19.33% (-590 bps); Q1 2026 15.20% vs 19.08% (-388 bps). Q2 2026 actuals are not yet loaded in VA. The CEO called Q2 a 'strong beat' and full-year earnings 'better than where we were in April' (doc 113196). The recovery depends on raw-material price-cost, utilization and Chemical Intermediates spreads, not on a new management plan.

disqualifier_reason: No catalyst in the 18-month window: CEO Costa since 2014, CFO unchanged, no acquisition, no investor day; only a CTO swap and one director. Margins are also partly commodity-price driven (raw-material price-cost and Chemical Intermediates spreads tied to the Mideast conflict, per the CEO).
verdict: Cheap and down 38%, but there is no leadership change, no acquisition and no multi-year margin target, and margin swings with raw materials and chemical spreads, so it is disqualified as a GXO setup.
open_questions: Will Eastman set multi-year targets (for example, at an investor day) for Kingsport methanolysis EBITDA and the circular platform?
How much of the FY2026 to FY2028 consensus margin recovery depends on Chemical Intermediates spreads vs the $125M to $150M of cost actions?
Is there any CEO succession planning after 12 years under Costa?
